text:
maria: FYI — just finished a call with Cobalt Health (large telemed customer). They asked for a Console feature to trace a tenant-level billing spike down to samples of traces, model version, region, and per-route latency. They want to be able to click a spike and get context (5 sample traces + token counts).

samir: they said this is a blocker for their internal audit. Sales thinks pilot would accelerate contract renewal. priority: high from their side.

ev an: can you paste their exact asks from the call? we should be specific for ACs.

maria: notes pasted below from customer rep: 
- show timeline with cost by tenant (24h, 7d, 30d)
- annotate spikes with top contributing routes and model versions
- from spike view be able to open 3-5 sampled traces correlated to requests that caused the spike
- see token counts (input/output) per sampled request and embedding vs generation cost attribution
- filters: model_version, region, route, status code
- access control: only tenant admins and our support can see tenant-level traces

olivia: quick thought — MVP could be: spike -> top routes + model_version list + link to sampled traces (no embedding vs gen breakdown). postpone per-token cost calc to phase 2. saves a lot of infra work. :thinking_face: 

jia: infra notes: sampling traces on demand is doable if we keep samples small. main concerns: PII in traces (customer wants request/response snippets), storage retention, and cross-tenant isolation if we surface tenant traces in Console. Need RBAC + scrub rules.

ev an: agreed. propose acceptance criteria for MVP: 
1) click on tenant cost spike shows timeline and top 10 contributing routes and model_versions
2) ability to open 3-5 sampled traces (HTTP headers redacted) tied to the spike window
3) surface median and p95 latency per route for the spike window
4) model_version + region visible in the trace metadata
5) RBAC: only tenant admins + redwood support role can view tenant traces
6) retention: 30 days for pilot; no long-term storage without opt-in

maria: customer asked for sample payloads in traces to debug prompt-level issues. we should confirm legal/POC before exposing.

jia: we can provide redacted snippets (first 200 chars) and a toggle for tenants in pilot to allow full payloads under NDA. adds implementation ~1 sprint.

samir: sales asks we aim for a 6-week pilot timeline to be useful for their QBR. is that realistic?

jia: with a focused MVP and one eng pair + small telemetry changes, 4-6 weeks is doable if we scope tight. need product to lock ACs and devex to mock the UX.

olivia: devex can ship a clickable mock + API shape in a week. sample API: 
``` 
GET /api/tenant/{id}/cost-spikes?window=24h
Response: [{spike_ts, top_routes: [{route, bytes, tokens, model_version}], sample_traces_link}]
\nGET /api/tenant/{id}/sample-traces?spike_ts=...&limit=5
Response: [{trace_id, timestamp, model_version, region, latency_ms, snippet}]
``` 

ev an: rollout plan proposal: pilot with Cobalt Health only -> collect feedback -> iterate -> open beta for other enterprise customers. Mark as gated by NDA + customer opt-in.

maria: blocking questions for legal/security: what scrub rules by default, and how do we display token counts without exposing content?

jia: suggestion: expose token counts as integers and snippets truncated; full payload behind customer opt-in + audit logs. also ensure traces are stored encrypted with tenant-specific keys.

telemetry-bot: New issue created: TICKET-9876 "Tenant spike -> trace drilldown (pilot)" assigned to jia. Priority: P2.

ev an: next steps: evan to write PRD with the ACs above + success metrics (time-to-resolution reduction, number of audits closed). olivia to deliver UX mock. jia to scope infra + security plan. maria to coordinate pilot sign-up with Cobalt. samir to follow up on contract language.

maria: awesome — I'll confirm pilot NDA and get back with acceptance from Cobalt by end of week. :thumbsup:

samir: thanks all.
